topComment.author: @Alucard-A-La-Carte
topComment.text:
The biggest problem with "Other M" is: it's both written and designed by people who are aware of what Metroid is, but feel like they have never actually played a Metroid game.

They know: cool female bounty hunter/soldier in power armor with cannon arm" and they wrote an INCREDIBLY tropey story around it. Centering on the female lead's trauma and daddy issues. They don't even really try to imply or indicate that: sometimes a trauma repeated feels just as terrifying as the first time. THAT would have been interesting!

The fact that "Dread" came along and did a really solid, borderline minimalist story just makes how needlessly melodramatic Other M is stand out even more. To me, Samus speaking Chozo out loud feels like a cooler, more earned character moment than "Samus overcoming her childhood trauma to kill the space pirate she's killed twice already."

replies.author: @DonWeaselYeehawEdition
replies.text:
​@BonJoviBeatlesLedZep a lot of the best Metroid Games are told thru subtext and gameplay. I think the Metroid Games have excellent stories and a great arc for Samus, but it's all implied. Obviously you could get more out of it if you read the Metroid Manga or read up on the lore, but if you want a game with more cutscenes or a more overt story, yeah. Metroid probably isn't the series.
Other M is a lot like Sonic 06. Is it doing unprecedented things for the franchise and its story? Yes. Are they good things? Absolutely not 💀

replies.author: @Alucard-A-La-Carte

@ShatteredObjects Hilariously, "Zero Mission" or "Dread" might be the way to go! If you MUST play a Metroid, they probably have the most good story (Other M certainly has the most...).

Otherwise, I'd say there's no real reason to. There are other games that take inspiration from Metroid and have a meatier story already, as the above posters said: Metroid is partially about the isolation and loneliness of being trapped on a truly alien world. The 2D Castlevania handheld games might be more what you're looking for, which would be ironic and fun.

topComment.author: @Bro3256
topComment.text: So regarding Ice Climber, I understand where most people are coming from in not enjoying the game but I feel what hurt it's chances the most is trying to approach the game like a more modern-ish platforming game when that is not how Ice Climber works. This doesn't have Super Mario Bros. controls since the game initially released in Japan on Famicom during a time when platforming games were still being figured out. This is also a very multiplayer centric game, even the TV commercial in Japan showcased two kids playing Ice Climber since that's very likely the intention, playing with a friend. Sure you can still enjoy it alone but half of the fun is climbing that mountain together. Also this is a good time to mention that the VS. System arcade version exists which later got ported to the Disk System and it's easily the most definitive version of Ice Climber, but it's not a version that would change opinions from the original cartridge release.
